title: Bridge an ISO-8583 request to a gateway and back

blocks.text: Your switch speaks ISO-8583; the payment gateway behind it speaks a REST API with its own names and formats. The bridge between them has two halves: turn the request into the gateway's request, and turn the gateway's reply back into the ISO-8583 response your acquirer is waiting for.
Write `GatewayBridge.toGateway(ISOMsg request, LocalDate today)`, returning a `PaymentRequest` with:

items: `amount`: field 4, an amount in minor units, with its decimal point (`000000100000` becomes `1000.00`);
`transactionType`: from the processing code in field 3, `000000` is `PURCHASE` and `200000` is `REFUND`;
`transactionDate`: field 13, `MMDD`, as `YYYY-MM-DD`, in the year of `today`.

blocks.text: Then write `GatewayBridge.toIso(ISOMsg request, GatewayResponse reply)`. It answers the request: a copy of it with the response MTI, and

items: when the reply's status is `SUCCESS`: field 39 `00` and the reply's transaction id in field 38;
otherwise: field 39 `05` and the reply's error message in field 63, with no field 38.
Field 13 carries no year. A month and day still ahead of `today` cannot have happened this year, so it belongs to the year before.
A processing code that is neither `000000` nor `200000` is refused with an `IllegalArgumentException`: sending the gateway a guessed transaction type moves money the wrong way.

cases.says: a purchase request becomes a gateway request with a decimal amount, an MM/YY expiry, its type and a full date
a success becomes a 00 response with the gateway's transaction id, a failure a 05 response with its error text
a transaction date later in the year than today is given last year
a processing code with no gateway transaction type is refused, not guessed
